title: Microtally Ledger pane and export slate for token-level attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a compact, scan-friendly ledger pane (Microtally) in the Redwood Console that surfaces token-level cost breakdowns, attribution metadata, and a lightweight export workflow (CSV/NDJSON). The goal is to give platform users fast visibility into which prompts, routes, or roles drove token spend and enable downstream chargeback or anomaly export workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Microtally pane renders per-route and per-user token sparklines and a per-row cost micro-summary within 300ms on typical console views
Users can filter by date range, model variant, and role and see immediate aggregation changes with clear row-level attribution labels
Export flow supports: row selection, full dataset export, and JSONL NDJSON line item export containing token metrics and attribution tags
Design provides responsive behaviors for desktop and tablet and defines accessibility roles for screen readers and keyboard navigation
Final designs include a performance tradeoff note describing when to lazy-load detailed attribution columns and when to show cached aggregates
design_notes: Pivot away from wide token tables; use condensed rows with affordances for inline expansion to reveal full attribution metadata
Introduce a ‘rate-band’ pill that summarizes pricing tier on each row to communicate slab-based costs alongside raw token counts
Sparklines show relative token usage across the date window; clicking a sparkline opens a micro-detail drawer with prompt snippet and KV-cache hit rate
Export slate should preserve role-based filters and include an option to redact prompt text for customers with PII concerns
Consider server-side precalculation for heavy aggregations to avoid client jank; prototype includes a lightweight 'preview' API response shape
Design includes a small in-line help CTA explaining unit cost vs. billable token definitions to reduce user confusion
decisions: Use compact accordion pattern rather than full modal for row expansion to reduce context switching
Default export format = CSV for accountants, plus NDJSON for engineering consumption
Show both nominal cost and effective cost after discounts in separate columns to keep attribution traceable
Defer role-aware column permissioning to a future iteration; current prototype will show all columns with explanatory tooltips
review_comments: PM: Add guardrail copy for large exports to recommend sampled exports for >1M rows (PM-221)
Eng: Confirm API shape for NDJSON includes stable attribution keys; ENG-4122 will provide contract by 2026-03-10
Design lead: Visual weight of sparklines needs tuning — reduce stroke and add neutral background band for better contrast
Security: Redaction toggle must be prominent and default to ON for customers with 'sensitive-data' label
next_steps: Incorporate ENG-4122 API contract changes into prototype by 2026-03-09
Run a 30-minute design review with PM and Eng on 2026-03-10 to confirm export UX and guardrails
Build accessibility checklist and hand off to FE with annotated Figma frames
Prepare a short demo script for the internal alpha on 2026-03-18
